port_waves.title: Crash, concurrency and multiplayer-correctness fixes (no new ids, no reset)
port_waves.rationale: Every item here is a bug checked in the 4.3 tree: the EncasedFireJet STATE crash, the shared carver RandomSource, chunk-loading cloud rain checks, static charm and flask state shared across players, boss loot loss through subList(28), ISTER allocating per frame, and the aurora shader crash. port_waves.title: Remaining 4.3-applicable bugfixes and data-only tweaks
port_waves.rationale: Bugfixes and JSON-level changes against code that 4.3 shares unchanged. Several (compat-tags, loot-table-fixes, spawn-cost-tuning, the stalactite rebalance) can ship immediately through KubeJS or a datapack without rebuilding the jar. The teleporter fixes prevent bedrock destruction and void spawns, and the knight_y fix only needs an extension of 4.3's conquered.js. Worldgen effects reach new chunks only.

port_waves.rationale: Built once and reused by the Lich Tower, Camp, Fallen Trunk, Hollow Trees, Courtyard and Final Castle hooks. The debug commands come first because they are the verification tool for everything after. The Beardifier bridge is the key 4.3-specific decision: 4.3's own doFill replaces the 1.21 tf-asm and PieceBeardifierModifier stack, which keeps the chunkgen overhaul out of scope.

BaseTFBoss and boss bars precede the Knight Phantom, Hydra and Lich work. The mob items are small and add only sound and loot ids.

port_waves.title: Mechanics and QoL that finish 4.3's WIP/NYI items
port_waves.rationale: 4.3 ships the Ore Meter and Magic Painting as NYI and the flasks as WIP. These features finish them and harden progression locks against block placement. All of them sit on existing 4.3 systems (shield capability, SimpleChannel, magic_paintings registry), so the risk is moderate and there is no worldgen impact.

port_waves.title: Cheap new blocks and items (Lich Tower prerequisites included)
port_waves.rationale: Mostly easy registrations that add new ids only. Most of the Lich Tower's block dependencies (terrorcotta, carpet, rope, finished fence, casket, candelabra with BE) land here, so the tower later becomes structure work only. The candelabra is the only existing block whose state changes; 4.3 never generates it.

port_waves.title: Worldgen content for newly generated chunks
port_waves.rationale: Everything here changes only ungenerated chunks. Bundle it into one release and do a single TF dimension reset plus Chunky pregen, rather than resetting per feature. Berry bushes come before oreberries and camps. The hollow-tree structure replaces 4.3's HollowTreeFeature and feeds the fallen-trunk exclusion zone. Highlands Underground uses 4.3's existing biome_layers (checked).

port_waves.title: Lich Tower and Lich
port_waves.rationale: The headline 4.8 content, scheduled once all infrastructure (wave 3) and decor blocks (wave 6) exist. Lich fight fixes shipped in wave 4, so this wave is the full rework. The tower is the single largest item (about 70h); plan a second TF dimension reset or accept that new towers appear only in unexplored areas.

port_waves.title: Construct update: drying racks, foods, camps, recipe-viewer polish
port_waves.rationale: Drying racks and tanned leather are prerequisites for Traveller's Gear, and camps need the jigsaw markers and berry bushes from earlier waves. The EMI and Jade/TOP work comes last so every category exists. Add copper_nugget and jerky tags to AlmostUnified and KubeJS here.

port_waves.title: Traveller's Gear sub-project
port_waves.rationale: About 150h, built entirely on Data Components, Data Attachments and around 10 tf-asm transformers. It needs a Mixin config in the fork. Isolated so it never blocks the earlier releases; item-display goes last as the lowest-value goggles modifier.

port_waves.title: Optional: density-shaped landmark terrain
port_waves.rationale: Cosmetic replacement of 4.3's working block deformers. Do it only if the Beardifier bridge has proven stable and another TF dimension reset is acceptable.

shared_infrastructure: Codec/API shim layer for 4.3: MapCodec/StreamCodec become Codec + KeyDispatchDataCodec.of / FriendlyByteBuf; Codec.withAlternative becomes ExtraCodecs.withAlternative; ResourceKey<LootTable> becomes ResourceLocation; BootstrapContext becomes BootstapContext. Interaction and gameplay APIs: ItemInteractionResult/useItemOn/useWithoutItem become use(); Holder<MobEffect> becomes MobEffect; ItemAbilities become ToolActions; PathType becomes BlockPathTypes; ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath becomes new ResourceLocation. Plus a Java 21 to 17 sweep (List.getFirst/getLast, SequencedCollection, switch patterns).

Beanification removal convention: @Component/@Autowired/@PostConstruct classes become static singletons or EventBusSubscribers, and reload listeners go through AddReloadListenerEvent. enumextensions.json becomes IExtensibleEnum.create where Forge 47 allows it (ItemDisplayContext, Rarity); otherwise drop it.

Item data layer (TFItemData) replacing Data Components with stack NBT or BlockEntityTag. Covers CASKET_DAMAGE, JAR_LID and CONTAINER, CANDELABRA_DATA, ORE_SCANNING/ORE_DATA/ORE_FILTER/ORE_RANGE, EMPERORS_CLOTH, and flask contents (keep 4.3's 'Potion'/'Uses'/'Breakage'), later the Traveller's modifier payloads. One place keeps NBT key names stable.

Entity and player data layer replacing Data Attachments with Forge capabilities or getPersistentData(). TFPlayerData holds the portal timer, flask tracking, banish flag and charm state; 4.3's shield capability stays. TFMobData holds multiplayer_fight participants, leash_pathfinder_override and the zombified-player profile. Includes clone-on-death and a client sync packet.

Networking: register each new packet on 4.3's TFPacketHandler SimpleChannel with a protocol bump. Packets: TFBossBarPacket, UpdateDeathTimePacket, SpawnCharmPacket, SyncQuestsPacket, StructureProtectionPacket v2, LifedrainParticlePacket, WipeOreMeterPacket and SetMasonJarItemPacket, with the Traveller's packets later.

Data-map replacement: one generic SimpleJsonResourceReloadListener, synced through OnDatapackSyncEvent where the client needs it, for 4.8's NeoForge DataMapTypes ominous_fire (entity conversions), magic_map_color and ore_map_color. Compostables go into ComposterBlock.COMPOSTABLES in enqueueWork.

Datapack and static registry plumbing via DataPackRegistryEvent.NewRegistry and RegistryBuilder: template_marker_handler, template_marker_handler_list, structure_speleothem_settings, chunk_blanket_processors and travellers_modifiers (datapack); template_marker_handler_type and chunk_blanket_type (static).

Resource migration rules for copied 4.8 data. Folder renames: structure/ to structures/, loot_table/ to loot_tables/, recipe/ to recipes/, advancement/ to advancements/, tags/block|item|entity_type to tags/blocks|items|entity_types. Content renames: c: tags to forge:, short_grass to grass, data-driven set_enchantments/set_components to 1.20.1 NBT loot functions. Keep 4.3 loot table ids (chests/*) for existing unopened chests.

4.8 NBT template import check (DataVersion 3955). 1.20.1's DFU leaves newer data untouched, and the scanned palettes (lich_tower, camp, courtyard, feature, final_castle) contain no post-1.20.1 vanilla blocks. Still check item stacks in block-entity NBT (the 1.20.5 'count' vs 'Count' key) and decorated pots (no inventory in 1.20.1), and re-save doubtful templates in a 1.20.1 dev world.

TF Beardifier bridge inside ChunkGeneratorTwilight.doFill (feature custom-density-terraforming): vanilla beard, CustomDensitySource and a TF IPieceBeardifierModifier interface, with no coremod because 4.3 owns the TF fill loop. Pass StructureManager into doFill and tune the scale against the unnormalized warp noise.

Registry remap policy: extend 4.3's TFRemapper (MissingMappingsEvent) for block and item renames. For registries without MissingMappings (structure piece types, processors), keep old ids registered as aliases to the new deserializer: TFNCTr, TFNCDu and TFNCSt map to CourtyardTerrace, and 4.3's stubs TFLTC2ST and TFLTSTRm become no-op pieces. Never port 4.8's removal of death_tome_spawner and empty_canopy_bookshelf.

Coremod strategy: keep 4.3's JS coremods (META-INF/asm), extend conquered.js for StructureStart.loadStaticStart (knight_y), and add armor.js for Emperor's Cloth. Add a Mixin config to the fork only for the Traveller's hooks: water walk, unrestrained, FOV, food exhaustion, slime block, MouseHandler#turnPlayer, PhantomSpawner and snowy grass.

Verification harness: a fixed-seed TF biome and landmark dump compared before and after worldgen changes, plus structure-debug-commands, run against a copy of the server seed before each release. Boot rule from AGENTS.md: reach Done with 0 FATAL, crash or watchdog entries.

Pack-side glue in this repo: rebuild local-mods/twilightforest-1.20.1-4.3-universal.jar from the fork. Add twilightforest:copper_nugget and jerky to config/almostunified and KubeJS tags, and ship compat tags through kubejs/server_scripts/tag_fixes.js.

The port would take 60-90h, change all TF terrain, require a TF dimension reset plus rewriting the stored level.dat generator, and break 4.3's landmark picking, troll clouds, canopy, glaciers and spawn lists, which all hang off ChunkGeneratorTwilight. The structure benefits (beards, CustomDensitySource) are reachable for about 18h through the doFill Beardifier bridge (custom-density-terraforming). Cost is out of proportion.

It brings no player-facing gain on 4.3. The useful part (progression and landmark wrapper types) is kept as landmark-wrapped-structure-types; structure_icon is not portable.

plan.savegame_summary: Waves 1-6 add only new registry ids, new NBT keys or new optional SavedData, and change worldgen only in ungenerated chunks, so they need no TF dimension reset. These items touch existing saved data in a controlled way. Candelabra: a player-placed 4.3 candelabra gains has_candle_1..3 and a block entity and loads empty; it is WIP in 4.3 and never generated. Jars: firefly, cicada and moonworm jars gain a BE with the default twilight_oak lid. Hydra: NumHeads changes to a bitmask, so a living Hydra may reload once with a different head set. spiral_bricks gains waterlogged=false. Naga Courtyard: keep TFNCTr, TFNCDu and TFNCSt registered as aliases, or old courtyards lose their terraces. Lich Tower: keep every old TFLT* piece type registered; 4.3's unused revamp stubs TFLTC2ST and TFLTSTRm become no-op aliases. Chiseled bookshelf: keep death_tome_spawner and empty_canopy_bookshelf registered and do not port 4.8's removal. Seed: removing seed.js must keep the identical seed value, or the landmark grid shifts. The Beardifier bridge makes terrain_adaptation take effect in the TF dimension for the first time, so structures that straddle old and new chunks can show a terrain seam. The worldgen waves 7 and 8 add berry bushes, oreberries, lakes, hollow-tree and fallen-trunk structures, Highlands Underground, carver changes, canopy and glacier blanketing, the Aurora Palace and Courtyard reworks, and the new Lich Tower. They only reach unexplored chunks, so on a pregenerated server a TF dimension reset (delete the twilightforest dimension folder, overworld untouched) followed by Chunky pregen is recommended once after wave 7 and again after wave 8. The overworld and the Skylands are unaffected. The excluded chunkgen overhaul is the only change that would have forced a full TF terrain reset and a level.dat generator rewrite.

missing.description: 4.8 replaces several hardcoded checks with tags that the plan does not mention. FireJetBlock reads the fluid tag #twilightforest:fire_jet_fuel (default #minecraft:lava). TrophyPedestalBlock reads #twilightforest:trophy_pedestal_activation_blocks. ThornsBlock skips damage for items in #twilightforest:immune_to_thorns. Tool repair ingredients become the item tags repairs_{fiery,giant,ice,ironwood,knightmetal,steeleaf}_tools; in 4.3, TwilightItemTier uses hardcoded Ingredient.of(TFItems.X), which is bad for AlmostUnified. Item tags trophies, banisters and ore_meter_targetable are added. #2306 (ee15cfe92) adds convention tags: canopy_bookshelf in bookshelves, mushgloom in mushrooms, the TF discs in music_discs, and sinister_spawner in features_cannot_replace.
missing.reason: Each item is a TagKey plus one is(tag) check, all of which exist in 1.20.1. On 1.20.1 the tags go in the plural tag folders and convention tags use forge: names. ForgeTier accepts a Supplier<Ingredient>, so Ingredient.of(TagKey) works. The repair tags let config/almostunified and kubejs/server_scripts/tag_fixes.js unify TF repair materials without hand-editing recipes, which matches the AGENTS.md rule.

misclassified.correction: Lower the effort by about 2h. The LiquidSettings.IGNORE_WATERLOGGING blocker does not need a waterlog-stripping processor. In 1.20.1 StructurePlaceSettings still has the boolean keepLiquids, with setKeepLiquids(boolean) and shouldKeepLiquids() (verified in the 1.20.1 client_mappings.txt), and 1.21's LiquidSettings enum replaced exactly that boolean. setLiquidSettings(IGNORE_WATERLOGGING) therefore becomes setKeepLiquids(false). The selection_priority and placement_priority blockers stay: 1.20.1 JigsawBlockEntity and SinglePoolElement have neither (verified), so read the raw jigsaw NBT from StructureBlockInfo.nbt.

(1) The plan says the leash 'uncooking' transformer is likely unnecessary on 1.20.1. That is wrong: 1.20.1 PathfinderMob still has tickLeash() and shouldStayCloseToLeashHolder() (verified in mappings), so leashed yard zombies would keep pathing back to the fence. Port PathFinderUnrestrainedByLeashTransformer as a JS coremod on PathfinderMob.shouldStayCloseToLeashHolder (AND the result with !persistentData flag at each IRETURN); add about 2h. (2) The painting_variant tags tower_paintings and tower_boss_paintings list 1.21-only variants (baroque, meditative, prairie_ride, unpacked, backyard, bouquet, cavebird, changing, cotan, endboss, fern, finding, lowmist, orb, owlemons, passage, pond, sunflowers, tides). On 1.20.1 the tag fails to load and LichTowerMagicGallery/LichTowerSegment.placePainting gets nothing, so prune the tags to 1.20.1 variants or mark the entries required:false. (3) 4.8 loot tables use enchanted_count_increase, copy_components and registry-keyed set_enchantments, and one table drops minecraft:bundle, which is feature-flagged off in 1.20.1. (4) Templates place twilightforest:skull_candle with the 4.8 blockstate candle count while 4.3 keeps the count in the BE, so those skulls load without candles. final_castle/temp/gazebo.nbt carries a neoforge:attachments fortification_shields entry that 1.20.1 ignores.

Only three new JS coremods are needed: HumanoidArmorLayer.renderArmorPiece, ElytraLayer.shouldRender and CapeLayer.render. The mob-detection part (ArmorHooks.modifyArmorVisibility on LivingEntity.getVisibilityPercent) maps onto Forge 47's LivingEvent.LivingVisibilityEvent#modifyVisibility, verified in the forge-1.20.1-47.1.70 sources, so no coremod is needed there. Effort drops by about 1.5h.

The savegame and world-impact risk is understated. Once the doFill bridge evaluates the vanilla Beardifier, every terrain_adaptation that 4.3 already declares takes effect in the TF dimension: bury on knight_stronghold, labyrinth, troll_cave and yeti_cave; beard_thin on dark_tower, final_castle, hedge_maze, lich_tower, naga_courtyard and quest_grove. yeti_cave would get bury plus 4.3's deformTerrainForYetiLair, a double deformation; 4.8 sets yeti_cave to none for this reason. The Labyrinth gets bury on top of its raiseHills mound. Either make the bridge honour only CustomDensitySource and TF IPieceBeardifierModifier pieces (ignore vanilla terrain_adaptation in the TF dimension), or ship 4.8's per-structure terrain_adaptation values (yeti_cave none; hedge_maze and final_castle beard_box) together with it. Otherwise wave 3 already changes landmark terrain in new chunks.

This is not self-contained. CandelabraBlock line 202 needs TFItems.EXANIMATE_ESSENCE and the #twilightforest:scepters tag (scepter-rework) to switch on the ominous state, so add depends_on ominous-fire-exanimate-essence and scepter-rework, or move the essence item and the tag earlier. The block also gains a 'lighting' NORMAL/DIM/OMINOUS state next to has_candle_1..3; savegame_impact should mention both.

No moonworm_jar exists in 4.3 or in 4.8. Only firefly_jar and cicada_jar become JarBlocks (FireflyJarBlock and CicadaJarBlock with the shared twilightforest:jar BE), plus the new mason_jar. The mason jar is also placed directly by 6 Lich Tower templates (5x5/potion, 7x7/desk, jar_study, shelved_jars, 9x9/cauldron_keep, tiered_spawner), not only from code.

Keep it easy, but put a verification gate in front of it. 4.3 seed.js stores the seed of the last WorldOptions constructed into TFDimensionSettings.seed, which LazyAreaContext and KeyBiomesLayer use. On the Arclight hybrid, extra WorldOptions instances (server.properties parsing, Bukkit or plugin worlds) can mean that value is not the overworld seed. Before switching to WorldUtil.getOverworldSeed(), log both values on the live server; if they differ, the switch shifts the biome and landmark map and the TF dimension needs a reset.

The classification is right, but port from HEAD (EntityEvents.adjustEntityHealthInMultiplayerFights, addQualifiedGroupPlayerIfNeeded and grantGroupAdvancementIfNeeded), not from the original PR commit. 5db77f784 (#1987) is the commit that introduced BaseTFBoss and rewrote every boss class, so cherry-picking it pulls in boss-base-class-refactor. 4.3's boss spawner BEs already call ForgeEventFactory.onFinalizeSpawn (verified), so MobSpawnEvent.FinalizeSpawn fires.

This also includes MiscEvents.addTomesToLecterns: using a Death Tome spawn egg on an empty lectern spawns a lectern-bound tome (setOnLectern). It is a few lines on PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickBlock; add about 0.5h.

Also missing is disableSkullCandleCreation, a new common option that gates makeSkullCandle in EntityEvents. 4.8's bossesSpawnDropChests is just the renamed 4.3 bossDropChests, so keep the 4.3 key. portalCreationPermission is listed here and again in progression-protection-overhaul, and disableIngredientSwitching is listed here and again in uncrafting-table-improvements; do each in one place only.

4.8 moved most chest loot tables out of chests/: aurora_cache, darktower_*, hill_1-3, labyrinth_*, stronghold_cache/room, tree_cache, troll_*, useless, well, fancy_well, foundation_basement and quest_grove_dropper now sit at twilightforest:<name>. New tables (hedge_cloth, fallen_trunk_loot, camp_tent, camp_pot, camp_armor_rack) also sit at the root. Keeping 4.3's chests/* ids is right, but every 4.8 structure JSON, template or Java constant copied later (TFLootTables, camp templates with LootTable NBT) must be remapped. The plan's 'twilightforest:chests/hedge_cloth' is a 4.3-convention id, not the 4.8 id.

ordering_issues: candelabra-overhaul (wave 6) references TFItems.EXANIMATE_ESSENCE and #twilightforest:scepters, which arrive in wave 8 (ominous-fire-exanimate-essence, scepter-rework). Move the exanimate_essence item and the scepters tag into wave 6, or move the candelabra to wave 8.

custom-density-terraforming (wave 3) switches on 4.3's existing terrain_adaptation values (bury and beard_thin) for every landmark in new chunks the moment it lands. That contradicts the 'waves 1-6: no worldgen change' statement in savegame_summary. Gate the bridge to CustomDensitySource-only until wave 7 (or 11), or plan the first TF dimension reset right after wave 3.

AlmostUnified and KubeJS unification of twilightforest:copper_nugget is scheduled in wave 9, but copper_nugget appears in wave 7 (oreberries). Add it to config/almostunified unify.json and modPriorities in wave 7, or Create and TF nuggets coexist for two releases.

knight-stronghold-fixes (wave 2) and progression-protection-overhaul (wave 5) both touch the 4.3 ProgressionEvents knight-stronghold hack ('pos.getY() >= sea level - 2 → unprotected'). 4.8 removed that hack only when per-piece protection landed (e9116aa11), so keep it in wave 2 and remove it in wave 5. Otherwise the stronghold surface becomes protected or unprotected inconsistently between releases.

weather-renderer-rewrite (wave 5) is ported from HEAD, where TFWeatherRenderer.renderLockedStructure consumes the per-piece boxes of StructureProtectionPacket v2. Add depends_on progression-protection-overhaul and keep that order inside wave 5.

lich-fight-fixes (wave 4) contains #2384 (c576062db), which calls FortificationShieldAttachment.addShieldBreakParticles and the new shield_break particle from fortification-shield-rework (wave 5). Move fortification-shield-rework into wave 4 or defer that line.

Do not copy 4.8 worldgen/structure/*.json for the new minor structures (hollow_tree, swamp_hollow_tree, fallen_trunk, camp, giant_house) before the codec changes are in. 4.8 nests decoration_clearance{} and controlled_spawns{}, replaces hint_mob with hint_creature, and adds structure_icon, while 4.3's LandmarkStructure and ProgressionStructure codecs expect flat chunk_clearance_radius, allow_biome_*, hint_mob and hint_item. Either port the codec reshape first (it belongs with avoid-landmark-modifier-v2 and landmark-wrapped-structure-types in wave 3) or hand-convert every JSON in waves 7 and 9.

Duplicated work across waves: 'Lich bombs spare items' appears in lich-fight-fixes (wave 4) and misc-event-tweaks (wave 5); portalCreationPermission appears in config-option-additions (wave 2) and progression-protection-overhaul (wave 5); disableIngredientSwitching appears in config-option-additions (wave 2) and uncrafting-table-improvements (wave 5). Assign each to one feature.

lich-tower-revamp (wave 8) depends on rising zombies spawning per piece through SpawnIndexProvider. In 4.3 structure spawns run through ChunkGeneratorTwilight.gatherPotentialSpawns and getMobsAt, not 4.8's LevelEvent.PotentialSpawns handler (EntityEvents.structureSpecialSpawns). Wire SpawnIndexProvider into 4.3's ChunkGeneratorTwilight.gatherPotentialSpawns as part of the tower work and budget it there.

addons.notes:
SOURCES / METHOD: I queried the Modrinth API (v2/search, project/{slug}/version) and CurseForge (search pages plus api.cfwidget.com for file lists). Latest 1.20.1 Forge and some 1.21.1 jars were downloaded read-only to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skytekx3-1201-server/b8d056e1-624d-50f6-b93c-43ffe737fcb9/scratchpad/addons/jars and jars21, and I checked only their mods.toml, mixin configs and bytecode string constants. Nothing was executed. Addon class references were checked against our local-mods/twilightforest-1.20.1-4.3-universal.jar, the 4.8 source tree, and the pack's Create 6.0.8, TConstruct 3.11.2 and Aether 1.5.2 jars. Upstream TF on CurseForge: 1.20.1 = 4.3.2508, 1.21.1 = 4.8.3345 (2026-10-28).

1) BLOCKER: TF version string. Our TF jar reports mod version "4.3": build.gradle has `version = CIRevision ?: mod_version`, gradle.properties has mod_version=4.3, and the manifest has Implementation-Version 4.3. Forge rejects every addon with a build-qualified range: D&V and ACOFI [4.3.1735,), Spartan TF [4.3.1893,), Cave Fix [4.3.2145,), Twilight Spellbooks and Goety Twilight [4.3.2508,). Fix: build the backport jar with -PCIRevision=4.3.2508.<n> (anything >= 4.3.2508). Stay on 4.3.x rather than 4.8.x; the 1.21-only addons pin [4.8,) anyway.

2) Freeze-list for the backport: 1.20.1 addons link these 4.3 symbols, which 4.8 deleted or renamed. Keep them, or add deprecated shims, or the addons crash with NoClassDefFoundError/NoSuchFieldError:
- util.TwilightItemTier (Spartan TF, TF&D, Cloudertinker)
- enums.TwilightArmorMaterial (Twilight Aether, Umbral Skies)
- init.TFDimensionSettings and world.registration.TFGenerationSettings, renamed in 118cdcb41 (Twilight Construct, Twilight Tweaks)
- block.TFLogBlock and item.recipe.TransformPowderRecipe (TF&D)
- util.EntityUtil (bf90b4a54) and block.TFChestBlock (17602f730) (boss respawn mods)
- network.ThrowPlayerPacket/TFPacketHandler and capabilities.* (Alternative Twilight, Cloudertinker)
- fields TFItems.CICADA/FIREFLY/MOONWORM (TF&D, D&V)

Mixin targets to keep stable: HedgeBlock, ThornsBlock and FinalCastleBossGazeboComponent (Lost Blocks). Keep 4.3 recipe ids/paths and tag names too, since datapack addons override by path.

3) Port these upstream fixes instead of using addons. TFCavesCarver: 939ceb293, 5c68bab19, 3b6def4c5, b0ee6b0db, 057fa40e7, e5eb085cb, d60cc688b, 51b29421c; this replaces Twilight Forest Cave Fix, whose @Overwrite would conflict. aurora.fsh: bdbc5c901 and 8bca68e8a; this replaces the Iris Xe and Intel fix mods.

4) Coupled decision: backporting the 4.8 boss rework (BaseTFBoss, rewritten Naga/Lich/Hydra/UrGhast/KnightPhantom) rules out Alternative Twilight 1.20.1, Boss Refactor and Boss Respawn, but enables porting Alternative Twilight Remastered and Spiced Twilight later.

5) Distribution: Modrinth-hosted addons go into modrinth.index.json and then tools/resolve_all.py. They are TF&D, Spartan TF plus spartan-weaponry-addon-toolkit, D&V, Lost Blocks, Farmer's Cutting TF, Apothic Category Compat, Twilight Treehouses and Twilight Aether; ARR is fine there because Modrinth hosts the files. CurseForge-only addons can go into local-mods/ only with a redistributable license: Twilight Construct (LGPL-2.1 source), Twilight Tweaks (LGPL-2.1), King of Twilight (MIT). Twilight Spellbooks is ARR and needs written permission from Mangelox before it can go in the .mrpack.

6) Recommended order: TF&D, Spartan TF, Twilight Construct, D&V, Lost Blocks, Farmer's Cutting TF, Apothic Category Compat, Treehouses, Twilight Aether, then Twilight Tweaks plus King of Twilight, then Twilight Spellbooks (after permission). Boot-test after each group (Done reached, 0 FATAL). Create: Shimmer is the only 1.21.1-only addon worth a real backport (Create 6 API is mostly shared; it also needs Create: Dragons Plus and permission for its ARR assets). Twilight Mobs Loots and Twilight Crossbow are optional small ports.
